headline: Pretraining Researcher Coxon Quits, Predicts Perilous AI Race
read: Jacob Coxon closes three years of pretraining work at OpenAI and Anthropic with a public warning that both labs race toward self-improving superintelligence at reckless speed. His resignation lands one day after Jacob Tsimerman's Mathematical AI Safety Institute opened its doors, turning a fresh Fields Medal into a Bay Area home for treating AI risk as solvable mathematics. Andrew Critch runs MAISI as Executive Director, pairing years of writing about catastrophic AI scenarios with an institute built to formalize them. Paul Christiano and Geoffrey Irving join the advisory panel, lending Alignment Research Center rigor and frontier-lab experience to a roster staffed mostly by mathematicians. Together the two stories pull the same thread from opposite ends: one researcher exits the labs entirely to sound an alarm from outside, while a fresh institute recruits mathematical talent to work the problem from within. Model releases dominated the earlier days of the week — GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Fable 5.1, and Muse Spark 1.3 — crowding out personnel news as newsrooms chased benchmarks instead. Coxon's exit reverses that pattern hard, pulling safety concerns back to center stage just as MAISI stakes its claim to a proof-based answer. Watch whether his departure becomes a rallying point for researchers weighing lab loyalty against public alarm, and whether MAISI's January 2027 cohort draws mathematicians away from frontier labs altogether. Nvidia's pending Hugging Face purchase still awaits formal leadership assignments, leaving founders Clem Delangue, Julien Chaumond, and Thomas Wolf in a holding pattern.
